## Introduction

The project was inspired by a post by [**Karina Samsonova**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karina-samsonova/) on linkedin.

The data is available on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vijayuv/onlineretail)

```{r}
#| label: import libraries
#| include: false
library(data.table)
library(tidyverse)

```

```{r import_data}
df <- read.csv(unz("online_retail_data.zip", "OnlineRetail.csv"))
colnames(df)
dim(df)
dt <- setDT(df)   # convert data.frame to data.table (by reference)
dt[, sort(unique(Country))]
dt[, .N, by = Country][order(-N)]
```

Filter out the country UK

```{r}
#| label: filtered UK only
#| echo: false
uk <- dt[Country == "United Kingdom"]
uk[, .N]         # number of rows
```

## Phase 1: Quick Data Quality Check

```{r}
#| label: phase1
#| include: false
#| echo: false

str(uk)
uk[, .N]
uk[, lapply(.SD, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))] #check for missing values in all columns
typeof(uk$CustomerID)
```

Column: Invoice Number

```{r}
uk[, .(
  missing = sum(is.na(InvoiceNo)),
  unique  = uniqueN(InvoiceNo)
)]

uk[grepl("^C", InvoiceNo), .N]
summary(uk)
head(uk)
uk[, InvoiceNo := as.factor(InvoiceNo)]
nlevels(uk$InvoiceNo)

```

Unique invoices are about 25900.

### Check for negative quantities (returns / cancellations)

```{r}
uk[, .(
  total_rows = .N,
  negative_qty_rows = sum(Quantity < 0),
  negative_qty_percent = round(sum(Quantity < 0)/.N * 100, 2)
)]

```

**Observation:**

-   Negative `Quantity` indicates returns or cancelled orders.

-   About 1.86 percent of the data was negative.

### see the invoices

```{r}
uk[Quantity < 0, .(InvoiceNo, StockCode, Description, Quantity)]

```

### Check for missing CustomerID (guest checkouts)

```{r}
uk[, .(
  missing_customer = sum(is.na(CustomerID)),
  missing_customer_percent = round(sum(is.na(CustomerID))/.N * 100, 2)
)]

```

About 26,96 percent of the customers id were missing

### Convert to time the invoice date column

```{r}
#| Validate data
#| echo: false
uk[, InvoiceDate := as.POSIXct(InvoiceDate, format="%m/%d/%Y %H:%M")]
```

## Phase 2: Clean Your Data

```{r}
#| label: filtered UK only
#| echo: false
uk <- dt[Country == "United Kingdom"]
uk[, .N]         # number of rows
dt$InvoiceDate %>% head()
uk[, Country := NULL]
names(uk)   # should no longer show "Country"
head(uk)

```

### Remove returns (InvoiceNo starting with "C")

```{r}
#| label:
uk <- uk[!grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo))]
# Should be zero cancellations now
uk[grepl("^C", InvoiceNo), .N]

# Confirm UK only
#uk[, .N, by = Country]

```

### Create `TotalSales` column

```{r}
#| label: Create a calculated field

uk[, TotalSales := Quantity * UnitPrice]

# Look at first few rows
head(uk[, .(InvoiceNo, StockCode, Description, Quantity, UnitPrice, TotalSales)])

# Summary of TotalSales
summary(uk$TotalSales)

uk[Quantity < 0, .N]


```

```{r}
neg_qty <- uk[Quantity < 0]
uk[Quantity < 0 & !grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo))]


```

“Some negative quantities exist without a corresponding C\* invoice; likely corrections or returns not properly logged.

```{r}
uk[Quantity < 0, .(
  total_negative = .N,
  standard_returns = sum(grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo))),
  anomalies = sum(!grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo)))
)]

```

**Explanation:**

-   `total_negative` → all rows with negative Quantity

-   `standard_returns` → negative rows **with InvoiceNo starting with “C”**

-   `anomalies` → negative rows *without C InvoiceNo*\*

    standard returns is zero because the invoice number starting with C has been removed.

```{r}
uk <- uk[Quantity > 0]
uk <- uk[!grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo))]
# Any negative Quantity left?
uk[Quantity < 0, .N]      # should be 0

# Any C* invoices left?
uk[grepl("^C", as.character(InvoiceNo)), .N]  # should be 0

# Quick row count
uk[, .N]                  # should be ~40–50K

```

## Phase 3: Analysis

### Analysis 1: Top 10 Bestselling Products

```{r}
#| label: Top 10 Bestselling Products
#| echo: false
top_products <- uk[, .(
  total_quantity = sum(Quantity)
), by = Description][order(-total_quantity)][1:10]

top_products

```

```{r}
top_products[, rank := 1:.N]
top_products

```

This shows **the 10 products with the highest units sold** in the UK after cleaning.

### Analysis 2: Top 10 Revenue Products

```{r}
#| label: Top 10 Revenue Products 
#| 
#| echo: false

top_revenue <- uk[, .(
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = Description][order(-total_revenue)][1:10]

top_revenue


```

```{r}
top_revenue[, rank := 1:.N]
top_revenue

```

### Analysis 3: Sales per hour

```{r}
#| label: Sales per Hour 
#| 
#| echo: false

uk[, InvoiceDate := as.POSIXct(
  InvoiceDate,
  format = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M",
  tz = "UTC"
)]

str(uk$InvoiceDate)

uk[, .(
  start = min(InvoiceDate),
  end   = max(InvoiceDate)
)]

uk[, hour := hour(InvoiceDate)]
uk[, .N, by = hour][order(hour)]
uk[, sum(TotalSales), by = hour][order(hour)]

```

### Analysis 4: Sales by Day of the Week

```{r}
uk[, weekday := weekdays(InvoiceDate)]
uk[, weekday := factor(
  weekday,
  levels = c("Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday")
)]
weekday_summary <- uk[, .(
  transactions = .N,
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = weekday][order(weekday)]

weekday_summary

```

```{r}
#| label: Sales by Day of Week 
#| 
#| echo: false
```

```{r}
uk[, month := format(InvoiceDate, "%Y-%m")]
monthly_summary <- uk[, .(
  transactions = .N,
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = month][order(month)]

monthly_summary
uk[, month_name := factor(
  format(InvoiceDate, "%B"),
  levels = month.name
)]

uk[, .(
  transactions = .N,
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = month_name][order(month_name)]

```

> *When do our bestselling products sell the most?*

Identify top 10 bestselling products (by quantity)

```{r}
top10_products <- uk[, .(
  total_quantity = sum(Quantity)
), by = Description][order(-total_quantity)][1:10]

top10_products

```

```{r}
uk_top10 <- uk[Description %in% top10_products$Description]

```

Analyze time patterns for top products

### By hour

```{r}
uk_top10[, .(
  transactions = .N,
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = hour][order(hour)]

```

### By weekday

```{r}
uk_top10[, .(
  transactions = .N,
  total_revenue = sum(TotalSales)
), by = weekday][order(weekday)]

```

perfect for product demand timing

## Phase 5: Recommendation

Insight: "Peak shopping hours are 12-2 pm, with 70% of daily sales occurring between 10 am-4 pm." Can it be based on weekdays?

Recommendation: 

"Schedule promotional emails to arrive between 10 am and 12 pm to catch the peak shopping window."
